Methods for nbreg objects

Source: R/methods-nbreg.R
nbreg-methods.Rd

Standard S3 methods for fitted negative binomial regressions returned by nbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.nbreg'
print(
  x,
  digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L),
  signif.stars = getOption("show.signif.stars"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("deviance", "pearson", "response"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
predict(object, newdata, type = c("link", "response"), ...)

Arguments

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Further arguments (currently unused).

object, x

An object of class "nbreg" (or "summary.nbreg" for the print method of the summary).

signif.stars

Logical; show significance stars?

type

For residuals(): "deviance" (default), "pearson" or "response". For predict(): "link" (linear predictor \(\eta\)) or "response" (mean \(\mu\)).

newdata

Optional data frame in which to look for covariates (and offset variables) for prediction. If omitted, the fitted values are used.

Value

coef() a named vector; vcov() a matrix; logLik() an object of class "logLik" with df = number of coefficients + 1 (for \(\theta\)), so that stats::AIC() and stats::BIC() work; fitted(), residuals() and predict() numeric vectors; nobs() the number of observations with positive weight; summary() an object of class "summary.nbreg" with a coefficient table of estimates, standard errors, z values and p-values.

Examples

data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
fit <- nbreg(art ~ fem + kid5 + ment, data = bioChemists)
fit
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = art ~ fem + kid5 + ment, data = bioChemists)
#> 
#> Negative binomial (NB2) regression, log link, fitted by IRLS
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)     femWomen         kid5         ment  
#>     0.39102     -0.23270     -0.13775      0.02937  
#> 
#> Theta: 2.241   (SE 0.2668 )
#> Log-likelihood: -1562.66 on 5 df
#> Iterations: 4 
#> 
coef(fit)
#> (Intercept)    femWomen        kid5        ment 
#>  0.39102467 -0.23269704 -0.13775445  0.02936915 
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))
#> (Intercept)    femWomen        kid5        ment 
#> 0.064526913 0.072183539 0.048153108 0.003116131 
logLik(fit)
#> 'log Lik.' -1562.664 (df=5)
BIC(fit)
#> [1] 3159.423
head(residuals(fit, type = "pearson"))
#>          1          2          3          4          5          6 
#> -1.0015086 -0.9276857 -0.9276857 -0.9296379 -1.0884583 -0.8147337 
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(fem = "Women", kid5 = 0, ment = 10),
        type = "response")
#>        1 
#> 1.571482
